summary_paragraph: The patient, a male with a history of ankylosing spondylitis on Simponi, asthma, hypertension, obstructive sleep apnea, and generalized anxiety disorder, was admitted for severe back pain that began during a bout of bacterial bronchitis. He reported worsening, pressure-like back pain radiating to the SI joints, poorly responsive to his home opioid regimen. His respiratory symptoms, including cough and shortness of breath, had improved with outpatient Augmentin and asthma management. In the hospital, IV ketorolac was effective in reducing pain, which returned to baseline over two days. He completed a full course of Augmentin, remained afebrile, and showed no signs of infection on labs or imaging. He was discharged home on his prior medications with instructions to continue Simponi, manage future flares with anti-inflammatories when possible, and follow up with his rheumatologist.
problems: Ankylosing spondylitis of unspecified sites in spine
Acute bronchitis due to other specified organisms
